newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Mayne says profit hit by interest,tax.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Mayne says profit hit by interest,tax.

text.p: Transport, healthcare and telecommunications group Mayne Nickless Ltd said on Monday the decline in its net profit before abnormals for the year to June 30, 1996 was largely attributable to higher interest costs and a higher effective tax rate.

"For the first time, the company's results reflect the full interest cost associated with its Optus investment together with interest on the debt used to fund the acquisition of Australian Medical Enterprises (AME)," the company said.
Mayne said also its effective tax rate had increased to 36 percent from about 29 percent in the previous year.
Earlier Mayne reported its net profit before abnormals fell 32.8 percent to A$85.1 million.

Mayne reported an abnormal loss of A$108.77 million which was primarily due to losses made on the divestment of a number of businesses including the sale of its armoured car business in the United Kingdom.

"Substantial organisational restructuring in line with the portfolio changes is well under way. Our prime objective is to enhance decisiveness and market flexibility and take full advantage of synergies in the group," managing director Bob Dalziel said in a statement.

Mayne said the strong performances from its Australian healthcare and security, French logistics and U.K. express businesses had been disguised by poor performance from its Belgium logistics and Australian express businesses.
Mayne said revenue for in its three core businesses, healthcare, time critical express and contract logistics all rose but earnings before interest and tax only rose for the healthcare division.
Earlier this year, Mayne said it would sell its 25 percent stake in telecommunications Optus Communications.
The company has said it intends to divest its stake through the float of Optus which is expected to occur later this year.
Mayne has said it intends to use the proceeds from the sale to fund growth in its core businesses, reduce debt and return surplus cash to shareholders.
At 2.30 p.m. (0430 GMT), Mayne Nickless shares were seven cents weaker at A$8.40.
